newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's Muoi to visit China.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's Muoi to visit China.

text.p: Vietnam said on Tuesday that Communist Party chief Do Muoi, the country's most senior official, would visit Beijing soon at the invitation of Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
An announcement carried by state media gave no details of the trip other than saying it would take place. A party official told Reuters it would happen within a week.

The official said the visit was aimed at promoting friendly relations. However, it will come in the wake of a dispute between Beijing and Hanoi over the positioning of a Chinese oil rig in contested waters of the South China Sea.
The Kan Tan 111 rig, owned by China's National Offshore Oil Corp, was moved into an area roughly midway between the coast of central Vietnam and China's Hainan Island in March.
The move prompted verbal sparring between the two neighbours. Although the rig was later withdrawn, subsequent talks in Beijing aimed at preventing a recurrence failed to find common ground.
Do Muoi, 80, last visited China in November 1995, four years after the two countries normalised diplomatic ties.
Vietnam and China have a long history of animosity, despite their ideological similarities.
The two clashed in a border war in 1979 which was followed by a lengthy period of frontier hostilities.
Vietnam refused to mourn the death earlier this year of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, the man seen as being responsible for that conflict.
